claims.text: Homogenized HfNbTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure with minimal secondary phases.
The single-phase BCC structure stabilizes the mechanical and thermal responses of HfNbTaTiZr at moderate temperatures.
Local lattice distortions persist at moderate temperatures in HfNbTaTiZr.
Some degree of short-range atomic ordering persists at moderate temperatures in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions and short-range atomic ordering restrict dislocation mobility.
A transition in the alloy's mechanical and thermal behavior occurs near 800°C.
Above approximately 800°C, thermal activation and increased atomic vibrations relax local lattice distortions and short-range ordering.
Relaxation of local lattice distortions and short-range ordering facilitates dislocation motion.
Below approximately 800°C, the alloy maintains near-constant yield strength relative to its room-temperature value.
Below approximately 800°C, the alloy maintains near-constant elastic modulus relative to its room-temperature value.
Below approximately 800°C, the alloy exhibits approximately linear thermal expansion.
Above approximately 800°C, yield strength decreases more rapidly.
Above approximately 800°C, elastic modulus decreases more rapidly.
Above approximately 800°C, the thermal expansion coefficient increases markedly and expansion becomes nonlinear.
At room temperature or below 500°C, lattice distortions and dislocation activity are minimally affected by thermal activation.
The proposed behavior applies to homogeneous, as-cast or homogenized, single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr under controlled conditions up to about 1000°C.
Alloys containing significant secondary phases may exhibit different behavior.
